## 1\. An exact multiscale finite-cut criterion

Let \(a\in\Gamma\)\. Choose finitely many nonzero vectors

\[
v_1,\ldots,v_k\in\mathbb N_0^d
\]

such that \(a+v_\ell\in\Gamma\) for every \(\ell\), and positive integers \(s_1,\ldots,s_k\)\.

Define

\[
\xi(n)=a+\sum_{\ell=1}^k n^{s_\ell}v_\ell.
\]

Choose a finite nonempty set of distinct offsets \(H\subset\mathbb Z^d\) such that \(a+h\in\Gamma\) for every \(h\in H\), and put

\[
D_n=\{\xi(n)+h:h\in H\}.
\]

All these states belong to \(\Gamma\)\. To see this, take paths \(a\leadsto a+v_\ell\) and \(a\leadsto a+h\)\. Since each \(v_\ell\geq0\), translating and repeating the first paths produces \(\xi(n)\), and translating the second paths produces \(\xi(n)+h\)\.

Define the coordinate growth degrees

\[
p_i=
\begin{cases}
\max\{s_\ell:(v_\ell)_i>0\},&\text{if some }(v_\ell)_i>0,\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

For \(h\in H\), put

\[
t(h)=\sum_i p_i h_i,
\qquad t_*=\min_{h\in H}t(h).
\]

Call a reaction \(r\) *eventually enabled at offset \(h\)* if

\[
a_i+h_i\geq(y_r)_i
\quad\text{for every }i\text{ with }p_i=0.
\]

These are exactly the reactions enabled at \(\xi(n)+h\) for all sufficiently large \(n\)\.

Let \(\partial H\) be the finite collection of pairs \((h,r)\) satisfying eventual enabling and

\[
h+z_r-y_r\notin H.
\]

Define

\[
\Delta=
t_*+
\max_{(h,r)\in\partial H}
\left(
\sum_i p_i(y_r)_i-t(h)
\right).
\tag{1}
\]

If \(\partial H\) is empty, take \(\Delta=-\infty\)\.

**Theorem — Multiscale finite-cut certificate**

If

\[
\boxed{\Delta<0,}
\tag{2}
\]

then the physical-time Poincaré gap on \(\Gamma\) is exactly zero. Moreover, a deterministic finite algorithm constructs a rational, finite-support witness \(f_j\) satisfying

\[
\operatorname{Var}_\pi(f_j)>0,\qquad
\frac{\mathcal E(f_j,f_j)}
{\operatorname{Var}_\pi(f_j)}
\leq\frac1j
\]

for every integer \(j\geq1\)\.

### Proof

Write \(w(x)=c^x/x!\)\. For each coordinate with \(p_i>0\),

\[
\xi_i(n)=b_i n^{p_i}+o(n^{p_i}),
\qquad b_i>0.
\]

Consequently, for each fixed offset \(h\),

\[
\frac{w(\xi(n)+h)}{w(\xi(n))}
\sim C_h n^{-t(h)},
\qquad C_h>0.
\]

For an eventually enabled reaction,

\[
q_r(\xi(n)+h)
\sim K_{h,r}n^{\sum_i p_i(y_r)_i},
\qquad K_{h,r}>0.
\]

Let

\[
W_n=\sum_{x\in D_n}w(x)
\]

and let \(B_n\) be the unnormalized outgoing stationary flux\:

B_n=
\sum_{\substack{x\in D_n,r\\x+z_r-y_r\notin D_n}}

## 2\. Finite exact witness construction and bit costs

The criterion above has a fully explicit witness-generation algorithm. No infinite numerical limit has to be evaluated.

For each \(h\in H\), define

\[
R_h(n)=
c^h\prod_i\frac{\xi_i(n)!}{(\xi_i(n)+h_i)!}.
\]

Because \(h_i\) is fixed, each factorial ratio is a finite product of polynomial factors or their reciprocals. Hence \(R_h(n)\) is an exactly computable rational function of \(n\)\.

Construct

\[
U(n)=\sum_{h\in H}R_h(n)
\]

and

\[
V(n)=
\sum_{\substack{h\in H,r\\h+z_r-y_r\notin H}}
\kappa_r R_h(n)(\xi(n)+h)_{y_r}.
\]

The falling factorial is a polynomial in \(n\), and is exactly zero whenever a source is disabled. Therefore

\[
\frac{B_n}{W_n}
=\frac{V(n)}{U(n)}
=\frac{P(n)}{Q(n)}
\]

for explicitly constructible integer polynomials \(P,Q\), after clearing denominators and choosing the sign of \(Q\) to make its leading coefficient positive.

Under the certified condition \(\Delta<0\),

\[
\deg P<\deg Q.
\]

Let \(q=\deg Q\), let \(q_q>0\) be its leading coefficient, and put \(S_P=\sum_k|p_k|\), where \(p_k\) are the coefficients of \(P\)\.

For positive integer \(n\), choose

\[
N_{\rm flux}(j)=
\max\left\{
1,\
\left\lceil\frac{2\sum_{k<q}|q_k|}{q_q}\right\rceil,\
\left\lceil\frac{4jS_P}{q_q}\right\rceil
\right\}.
\]

For all \(n\geq N_{\rm flux}(j)\),

\[
Q(n)\geq\frac{q_q}{2}n^q,\qquad
\frac{P(n)}{Q(n)}\leq\frac1{2j}.
\]

The case \(P\equiv0\) is handled directly.

To control the stationary mass without computing \(Z_\Gamma\), select a coordinate \(i\) that grows along \(\xi(n)\)\. Then

\[
\xi_i(n)+h_i\geq n
\]

for every \(h\in H\) and integer \(n\geq1\)\.

Put \(C=\sum_i c_i\) and \(K=\lceil2c_i\rceil\)\. The elementary factorial-tail bound gives

\[
W_n\leq |H|\,2^{\lceil2C\rceil+K-n}
\qquad(n\geq K).
\]

Since \(Z_\Gamma\geq w(a)\), an explicit integer \(N_{\rm tail}\) can be obtained from the denominator of the reduced rational number \(w(a)\), ensuring

\[
n\geq N_{\rm tail}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
W_n/Z_\Gamma\leq\tfrac12.
\]

Set

\[
n_j=\max\{N_{\rm flux}(j),N_{\rm tail}\},
\qquad
\boxed{f_j=\mathbf1_{D_{n_j}}.}
\]

Substitution into (4) proves

\[
\frac{\mathcal E(f_j,f_j)}
{\operatorname{Var}_\pi(f_j)}
\leq
\frac{1/(2j)}{1-1/2}
=\frac1j.
\]

The entire construction uses integer and rational arithmetic.
